messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: service=redwood-runtime-gpu-pool-eu, alert=CUDA_ALLOC_FAILURE_RATE_HIGH, count=42, severity=high, runbook=https://redwood/intranet/runbooks/gpu-oom

pagerduty: Triggered by escalation policy 'GPU Runtime Oncall' -> paging sara.chen

sara.chen: ack'd. I'm oncall, looking now. any customer-facing errors showing? :eyes:

ben.jacobs: @sara.chen seeing spike in cuda_alloc_failures on node pool eu-gpu-3, also nvml reports mem_used jumping then kernel errors. logs attached to the incident.

kai: pushing quick telemetry: cpu/gpu metrics show 90%+ GPU mem utilization across 3 pods in the pool, but only 60% user-visible traffic. suspicious prefetch or kv-cache growth.

lee.martin: support-bot reported 3 customer sessions with LLM generation errors (502 / 'CUDA error: out of memory'). ticket IDs #2451 #2452 #2453. low volume but same error class.

sara.chen: ok plan: 1) drain pods from eu-gpu-3 to stop new allocations 2) trigger pool autoscale + increase reserve if autoscaler allowed 3) fallback traffic -> smaller quantized model variant in region-eu-1 to preserve latency. executing now.

ben.jacobs: running drain: kubectl -n runtime cordon eu-gpu-3 && kubectl -n runtime drain eu-gpu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30

ben.jacobs: drain started - some pods failing termination because prefetch threads stuck. attaching logs: ```
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] kvcache_prefetcher: enqueued seq=4021 size=128MB
[2026-03-15T14:02:31Z] alloc.cu: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T14:02:31Z] runtime: kernel panic signal SIGSEGV in module attention_kernels.cu
```

kai: I'm triggering an emergency autoscale bump for dedicated-eu pool: API call: POST /admin/pools/eu/gpu/scale {"target_instances":8} -> accepted. should start provisioning in ~2m.

incident-bot: Note: autoscale action recorded in incident timeline by @kai.

sara.chen: can we force degrade model variants for the affected customer routes? Use routing tag 'fallback-compact' for chat.predict on route /v1/chat/complete?

ben.jacobs: yes, updating routing policy: ```yaml
route: /v1/chat/complete
selector: pool=eu
actions:
  - fallback_model: redwood-3b-int8
  - priority: prefer-local=false
```

ben.jacobs: applied. starting to see drop in token allocation on heavy pods.

lee.martin: informing support: "We're routing traffic to compact variants while we stabilize the EU GPU pool. Some customers may see slightly different output quality." sending now.

support-bot: Message posted to customer #2451: "We're investigating CUDA OOMs affecting a small percentage of requests in EU. We're routing to compact model variants and expect reduced errors within minutes."

kai: nvml snapshot shows one node with leaking driver memory: gpu0 persistent mem climbing even after workloads scaled down. suspect kernel-driver leak after recent runtime kernel update.

sara.chen: good catch. we should remove eu-gpu-3 from rotation permanently until patch. create a short-term mitigation: taint node with dedicated=isolated:NoSchedule and mark for reprovision.

ben.jacobs: taint applied and node marked for reprovision. also collecting coredump; uploading to s3://redwood-debug/eu-gpu-3/8472109999.tar.gz

kai: opening escalation to eng-runtime: @lee.martin can you please ping runtime infra oncall to get kernel-driver patch? (cc @ben.jacobs)

lee.martin: pinged runtime-infra oncall. they replied: "we're looking at a new nv driver that could address a leak, need 30-45m to validate and coordinate rolling reprovision."

sara.chen: next steps timeline: 0-5m drain + fallback -> in progress; 5-20m autoscale + routing -> in progress; 20-60m reprovision node + driver test -> pending; customer impact: small portion of requests saw 502s, now routed, expect resolution within 1h. I'll update status page.

pagerduty: Incident status updated: acknowledged by sara.chen, severity=high, impact=partial degradation for EU region. Escalation to eng-runtime escalated.

ben.jacobs: quick diagnostic snippet I ran: ```bash
# show processes holding GPU memory
nvidia-smi pmon -c 1 -s um
# top of erroring container
kubectl logs pod/runtime-worker-77 -n runtime --tail=200 | grep -i cuda
```

kai: note: observe KV cache growth on routes with long-context customers. filing a ticket to cap prefetch size per-route later today to avoid recurrence.

sara.chen: oncall handoff: my shift ends in ~35m, @ben.jacobs will take follow-up once I'm off. ben can you confirm you'll own remediation and status updates at +35m?

ben.jacobs: will do. I'll watch autoscale + reprovision progress, and coordinate with runtime-infra for the driver rollout.

lee.martin: Support update posted to status.redwood.com: "Partial degradation in EU affecting some model generations. Mitigation in progress. No broad customer data loss. We'll post more details within 30 minutes."

support-bot: Customer #2452 updated: "Thanks for the heads-up. Appreciate the fallback routing." :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Resolution notes pending. Please include final remediation steps and follow-up action items (driver rollback/rebuild, kv-cache prefetch cap, alert tuning).

sara.chen: adding follow-ups: 1) runtime: validate nv driver and reprovision images 2) runtime: add node health probe for persistent gpu mem growth 3) product: consider routing policy default for fallback-compact on heavy-context routes 4) ops: add alert to distinguish kernel-driver leaks vs normal OOM spikes

ben.jacobs: copying final logs to incident summary. I'll post a closure update when autoscale finished and node reprovision completed. thanks all. :heart:

lee.martin: thanks team. handoff acknowledged.

support-bot: Incident ticket updated: severity lowered to monitoring after routing applied and error rates reduced by 90%

sara.chen: leaving channel — handing to @ben.jacobs. please escalate if error rate climbs back above threshold.

ben.jacobs: ack, taking over. continuing watch.
